sections.h2: Where Fulton County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
The Real Estate Division of the Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts records and indexes deeds for Fulton County property. It also handles lien filings, plats, condominium floor plans, military discharges, partnerships, trade names and Uniform Commercial Code filings.

The Deeds and Records Room is on the ground floor of the Lewis Slaton Courthouse in Atlanta and holds instruments reaching back to the early 1800s. The Real Estate Recording customer service line is (404) 613-5313. Mail for the Record Room goes to 136 Pryor St., CG13, Atlanta, GA 30303.

Paper documents are processed within four weeks of receipt. Documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state clerks' authority are processed in two to three business days. The clerk's site has a land records update page that reports processing progress, so check it when timing matters for a closing.

Once recorded and processed, the original documents come back to you by mail. Because paper and electronic filing differ so much in speed, ask whoever runs your closing how they plan to submit the deed. The clerk names three vendors: SimpliFile, eRecording Partners Network and Corporation Service Company (Ingeo).

A deed or any other instrument pertaining to real estate costs $25.00. Each cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment is also $25.00 per instrument listed on the filing. The Real Estate Division takes cash, business checks and money orders, and no credit cards for real estate transactions.

Fulton County clerk real estate fees, schedule dated July 1, 2024

The schedule has other recording lines, such as $5.00 for the first page of an instrument not otherwise specified. Ask the division which line fits your document before you send payment.

The clerk's office also issues notary commissions: $55.00 in person for a new or renewed commission, or $60.00 for a renewal by mail. A certificate of authority is $2.00.

sections.h2: Georgia transfer tax on a Fulton County sale
sections.html:
No deed gets recorded here until transfer tax is settled. The state charges a flat $1 on the first $1,000 of price, then a dime for each further $100 or fraction thereof.

The seller owes it by default, and a clause in the sales contract can hand it to the buyer. The PT-61 declaration is filed online through the clerks' authority, whose support line for filers is (800) 304-5174. If you wonder whether a transfer is exempt, ask this clerk.

sections.h2: What to have ready when you record
sections.html:
Most sellers never visit the clerk themselves, because the closing agent files the deed. It still helps to know what goes into the package.

  1. The signed deed, with the transfer tax declaration (the PT-61) filed online and the tax settled.
  2. Payment of the $25.00 recording fee, in a form the division accepts: cash, a business check or a money order. Do not plan on a credit card.
  3. Separate $25.00 charges for any cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment that goes in with the deed.
  4. A return address, since the original comes back by mail after processing.

If your closing agent uses an eRecording vendor, the vendor handles the submission and the two to three business day timeline applies. Ask which route is planned so you know when to expect the recorded copy.

Visit the Deeds and Records Room and use its computer lab, or search from home on the state authority's website, which costs $5 for four hours of access. Staff cannot do legal research by phone. To check a deed or lien index you either search it yourself or hire a title search company.

  • Certified copies must be ordered through eCertification at ecert.gsccca.org, which delivers a secure PDF by email after you approve payment.
  • Plain copies can be ordered the same way, around the clock.
  • By mail, send a letter naming the document type and its book and page number. The clerk's FAQ lists $1.00 a page for plain copies and $2.50 for the first certified page plus $0.50 for each added page.

If you cannot find a recorded cancellation of your old loan, ask your servicer for a copy and then check the index.

Tax liens filed by a state or local agency have their own pricing: $5.00 for page one, $2.00 for every page after, and $2.00 more for each cancellation, release, notice or withdrawal that references the original. Federal tax liens, materialman's liens, lis pendens and writs of fieri facias fall under the $25.00 lien and General Execution Docket line instead.

Owners who take a county tax appeal to superior court pay a $25.00 County Tax Appeal line in the clerk's court-cost table. The assessor's notice and the board that hears the first appeal come before that step, so start with the county's assessment office and the notice it mailed you.

Transfer tax is billed on top of every figure above. If the deed is the only thing you are recording, the $25.00 fee and that tax are the two numbers to plan around.

sections.h2: Intangible recording tax and foreclosure sales
sections.html:
A lender financing the buyer's purchase pays a separate intangible recording tax, which the state prices at $1.50 for every $500 of the note, with part of $500 counted as a whole.

Foreclosure sales are a separate public process. Properties sold in Fulton County are advertised once a week for four weeks in the legal notices of Fulton Neighbor Newspapers. Auctions run monthly on the first Tuesday, with bidding from 10:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse steps.

  • If you are behind on a mortgage, get the scheduled sale date from the servicer in writing.
  • A sale that has already been advertised still leaves time to sell the property or work out a plan, but that window is short.

Fulton County has 1,098,791 residents and 534,663 housing units. Owners occupy 54.3 percent of homes, so rentals are a big slice of the market. The median owner-occupied home is worth $458,800, and median gross rent is $1,732 a month.

If you are selling a rental or an inherited house, line up the recorded deed history before listing. A missing cancellation or an old lien is easier to clear before a buyer's title search finds it. A cash buyer still needs a clean recorded chain, so the same cleanup applies.

faqs.q: Which Fulton County office takes a deed for recording?
faqs.a: The Real Estate Division of the Fulton County Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts in Atlanta, or an approved eRecording vendor. The customer service number is (404) 613-5313.

faqs.q: How much is the Fulton County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: The schedule dated July 1, 2024 lists $25.00 for a deed or any instrument pertaining to real estate, plus $25.00 for each cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment.

faqs.q: Does the Fulton County clerk take credit cards for real estate recording?
faqs.a: No. Pay with cash, a business check or a money order.

faqs.q: How quickly does Fulton County record a deed?
faqs.a: Paper documents are processed within four weeks of receipt. Documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state authority are processed in two to three business days.

faqs.q: When are foreclosure sales held in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Monthly, on the first Tuesday, with sales running 10:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse steps. Notice appears weekly for four weeks beforehand.
